data.current_description: Runs recognition synchronously on one image and returns the extracted data. One credit is charged only when the scan is billable, drawn from the month's free credits first and from paid credits once those are used up. A scan is billable when the document type was determined and at least one of an MRZ with valid checksums, five or more visual-zone fields, or a decoded barcode was read. Sandbox keys are never charged: `sk_sandbox_public` recognizes the image it is sent, free, within its lifetime allowance, while a registered account's own `sk_sandbox_...` key is answered from a fixed synthetic specimen. The result is written down only when the retention window resolved for the request is above zero: `options.retain_hours` when the request names one, otherwise the account's own history-retention setting. Send `retain_hours: 0` to have nothing stored at all, so there is nothing to read back later. Besides an API key, this operation accepts a client token from `POST /v1/client-tokens`, so a browser or an app can send a scan without holding the key: the scan is billed and stored exactly as the issuing key's would be, and every request presented with the token spends one of its uses, whatever its outcome.
data.summary_suggestion: Synchronously recognize and extract document data
data.description_suggestion: Runs synchronous document recognition on a single image and returns extracted data including document type, holder information, MRZ, and visual-zone fields. Charges one credit only when billable (document type determined and at least one of: valid MRZ checksums, 5+ visual-zone fields, or decoded barcode). Free credits (100/month) are drawn first, then paid credits. Supports both API keys and short-lived client tokens. Results are stored based on retention window (`options.retain_hours` or account default); send `retain_hours: 0` to skip storage. Sandbox keys are never charged and use synthetic specimens.

data.current_description: The account's scans, most recent first, as history rows, one page at a time. Only scans made with a live key and kept under a non-zero retention window are listed, and only while that window lasts; a sandbox key sees an empty list. `limit` sets the page size (1 to 100, default 100) and `cursor` continues from the `next_cursor` of the previous page, which is null on the last one. The full result of any one scan is read back through `GET /v1/scans/{id}`.
data.description_suggestion: Retrieves paginated history of the account's scans, most recent first. Only scans created with a live key and retained under a non-zero retention window are included; sandbox keys return an empty list. Pagination parameters: `limit` (1-100, default 100) controls page size, and `cursor` (from previous `next_cursor`) continues pagination. Returns `next_cursor: null` on the final page. For complete scan details including extracted data, use `GET /v1/scans/{id}`. Note: scans are only listed while within their retention window.

data.current_description: Deletes a scan the account still holds, before its retention window would have ended: the stored result, its history row and its thumbnail. It cannot be undone – the scan can no longer be read, listed or replayed through an `Idempotency-Key`. The credit the scan drew is not returned, and the period's usage counters keep counting it. Only a live key deletes, and only its own account's scans; anything else – an unknown id, another account's scan, a scan whose window has passed, a sandbox key – is `404`.
data.description_suggestion: Permanently deletes a stored scan before its retention window expires, removing the scan result, history row, and thumbnail. This action cannot be undone – the scan cannot subsequently be read, listed, or replayed via `Idempotency-Key`. Important: the credit consumed by the scan is not refunded, and usage counters continue to reflect the scan. Only live keys can delete, and only their own account's scans; returns `404` for unknown IDs, other accounts' scans, expired retention windows, or sandbox key attempts.

data.current_description: Issues a client token: a short-lived credential that can call `POST /v1/scans` and nothing else. Call it from your server with your API key and hand the token to a browser or an app, which then sends the scan straight to this API without ever holding the key. A token lives 300 seconds and allows 1 scan request unless the body asks otherwise; send `{}` to take the defaults. Its scans are billed and stored exactly as the issuing key's would be, a sandbox key issues sandbox tokens, and revoking or deleting the key ends every token it issued. The token is returned once and only its hash is kept.
data.description_suggestion: Issues a short-lived client token that enables secure document scanning from browsers or apps without exposing your API key. The token can only call `POST /v1/scans` and nothing else. Default behavior: 300-second lifetime, 1 scan request allowed (customize via request body). Scans performed with the token are billed and stored identically to scans from the issuing key. Sandbox keys issue sandbox tokens. Important: the token is returned only once; only its hash is stored. Revoking or deleting the issuing key invalidates all its tokens.

data.current_description: Issues a client token: a short-lived credential that can call `POST /v1/scans` and nothing else. Call it from your server with your API key and hand the token to a browser or an app, which then sends the scan straight to this API without ever holding the key. A token lives 300 seconds and allows 1 scan request unless the body asks otherwise; send `{}` to take the defaults. Its scans are billed and stored exactly as the issuing key's would be, a sandbox key issues sandbox tokens, and revoking or deleting the key ends every token it issued. The token is returned once and only its hash is kept.

Token lifetime is 300 seconds with 1 scan request allowed by default; customize via request body. Scans performed with the token are billed and stored identically to key-issued scans. Returns the token once; only its hash is stored server-side. Sandbox keys issue sandbox tokens. Revoking or deleting the issuing key invalidates all its tokens.
